claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child - Alex, who's 10 years old. I'm looking to see if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 10 years old.

Let me ask you: **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex.

**Does Alex live with you, or if not, are you contributing financially to Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. I do help out a bit though - I contribute some money towards things for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. It's important to understand the full situation here.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions? Also, does Alex live with someone else who might be claiming Child Benefit for him?**

(Just to note: To qualify for Child Benefit when a child doesn't live with you, you generally need to be paying at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment - which is currently around £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child - towards their upkeep.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I contribute about £20 a week towards his needs - things like clothes and bits and pieces he needs. 

Yes, his mum has him living with her. I'm not sure if she's claiming Child Benefit for him or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

**Is Alex's mother currently claiming Child Benefit for him?** 

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child. If she is claiming it, you wouldn't be able to claim it as well unless she stopped her claim first and you both agreed that you should claim instead.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure to be honest - I'd have to check with her about whether she's claiming it or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me explain the situation based on what you've told me so far.

To be eligible for Child Benefit when a child doesn't live with you, you need to be contributing at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards the child's upkeep. The current Child Benefit rate is approximately £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child.

You mentioned you contribute about £20 per week towards Alex's needs. This is slightly below the threshold that would typically qualify you for Child Benefit when the child doesn't live with you.

However, there's another crucial factor: **only one person can get Child Benefit for the same child**. Since Alex lives with his mother, she would typically be the one claiming Child Benefit for him. If she is already claiming it, you would not be able to claim it at the same time.

Before I can give you a final determination, I need to know: **Can you find out from Alex's mother whether she is currently claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Alright, let me give her a call quickly... 

*pause*

Okay, I just spoke with her. She said she's not claiming Child Benefit for Alex - she never applied for it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for checking with her. That's helpful to know.

So Alex's mother is not claiming Child Benefit for him. However, as I mentioned, when a child doesn't live with you, you need to be contributing at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards their upkeep to qualify.

Let me ask: **Would you be able to increase your contributions to at least £25.60 per week (or the equivalent amount monthly or as a lump sum) to meet the Child Benefit threshold? Or do you already contribute more than £20 per week when you include all forms of support like pocket money, food, presents, and any financial contributions towards his accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, £20 a week is what I manage to contribute - that's all I can afford at the moment. That covers everything I help with for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being clear about your circumstances. I now have enough information to make a determination about your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 10 years old (under 16, so meets the age requirement)
- You live in the UK
- Alex doesn't live with you - he lives with his mother
- You contribute £20 per week towards his upkeep
- His mother is not claiming Child Benefit for him

The key issue is that when a child doesn't live with you, you need to be contributing **at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment** towards their upkeep to qualify. The Child Benefit rate for an eldest or only child is approximately £25.60 per week, and you're contributing £20 per week.

Unfortunately, this means your contribution falls short of the threshold required to qualify for Child Benefit when the child doesn't live with you.

conversation.text:
**Eligibility Decision: You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**

I'm sorry to inform you that based on your current circumstances, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. 

**The reason:** Since Alex doesn't live with you, you would need to be contributing at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (approximately £25.60 per week) towards his upkeep. Your current contribution of £20 per week falls below this threshold.

**However, there are options:**
- If you were able to increase your contributions to at least £25.60 per week (or the equivalent monthly/lump sum amount), you could become eligible
- Alternatively, since Alex lives with his mother and she's not currently claiming, she would likely be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex if she chose to apply

I know this may not be the answer you were hoping for. If your circumstances change in the future, you may want to reassess your eligibility.
